newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower, key bank stocks lead fall.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower, key bank stocks lead fall.

text.p: Large capitalised banking stocks led the market's fall on worries that domestic interest rates will remain firm, dealers and analysts said.
"There are concerns that interest rates will remain high," said a banking analyst at a Malaysian brokerage.

At the close, the key Composite Index was down 7.96 points or 0.74 percent to 1,069.96. The Second Board index fell 1.43 to 568.73. The KLSE Financial Index was down 89.22 or 0.98 percent to 9,018.32.
Maybank fell 1.0 ringgit to 25.25 ringgit and Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank by 40 cents to 16.0.
Malaysian rates have edged up in recent weeks, with expectations that higher average interbank rates this month could lead to another round of hikes in base lending rates.
But analysts said the interbank rates should have peaked this month. "Interest rates are easing a bit. The recent hikes are temporary," said Mohaiyani Research's Amin Abdul Manap.
Bucking the weak financial trend was MBf Capital, which rebounded strongly from its Tuesday plunge.
"The swing in MBf Capital is scary," said an institutional dealer at Jardine Fleming. MBf stock rose 46 cents or 10.9 percent to 4.68, after falling 98 cents on Tuesday.
